previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old female with a history of type 1 diabetes, stage 4 chronic kidney disease, prior pancreas and kidney transplants, and recent mechanical mitral valve replacement was admitted for shortness of breath due to a large left pleural effusion. She had an elevated INR from warfarin, requiring reversal with vitamin K and bridging with heparin before a thoracentesis could be performed. The procedure was successfully completed, removing 1.2 liters of fluid, and her breathing improved. However, imaging showed reaccumulation of the effusion and new left lower lobe consolidation, prompting antibiotic treatment and diuretic adjustment for underlying heart failure. Her INR was stabilized, warfarin was restarted, and she was discharged with follow-up planned for ongoing management of heart failure, anticoagulation, and transplant-related complications.

Discharge Instructions:
Ms. ___-

It was a pleasure taking care of you at ___ 
___.  You came to the hospital because of ongoing 
abdominal pain, worsening lower extremity swelling and fluid 
weeping, as well as shortness of breath with exertion.  

You had a transthoracic echo performed, which is an ultrasound 
of the heart.  The imaging study showed possibly some decrease 
in cradiac function, however this may have been due to inter 
operator  variability and not necessarily worsening heart 
function.  We adjusted your diuretics, and added a new 
medication called METOLAZONE to your medication regimen.  This 
medication should be taken ___ hour before taking your oral 
TORSEMIDE, as it works ___ with METOLAZONE.

Your abdominal pain has been ongoing for several weeks.  Your 
gastroenterologist was contacted and your history was discussed. 
 Your symptoms are likely due to MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA, a 
condition where vascular disease of the gut causes symptoms of 
pain.  Much like coronary vascular disease can lead to chest 
pain, mesenteric ischemia can lead to abdominal pain.  Continue 
to take your cardiovascular medications.  Symptomatically, you 
can avoid symptoms by eating small meals to reduce the need for 
increased blood flow to the gut.  Also, avoid very vigorous 
activity within 2 hours of eating, as this can cause decrease 
blood flow to the gut and lead to symtpoms.  Continue to take 
your constipation medications to maintain good intestinal flow.  
You have a follow up appoinment with your gastroenterologist in 
several weeks to further discuss your symptoms.  

For your leg swelling, please wear ___ stockings to keep your 
leg swelling minimal.

Regarding your heart valve, your INR was above therepeutic range 
(5.5, goal 2.5-3.5).  Please have your INR checked tomorrow.  If 
your INR is less than 5.5, please lower your warfarin dosing to 
4 mg a day.  Please have your INR followed up with your PCP 
___ 2 - 3 days until you are within therepeutic range to avoid 
under or over treating.

Regarding your systolic heartfailure and renal failure, weigh 
yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more than 3 
lbs.
